turnaround_reason: Stock collapsed in 2025 on ELEVIDYS safety signals (fatal acute liver injury in gene-therapy patients), a label update, and a strategic restructuring. It is recovering as commercial DMD franchise and cost cuts restore profitability, with an enhanced-immunosuppression protocol aimed at de-risking the liver-injury issue.
bullish_points: Q1 2026 blew out estimates: adjusted EPS $3.16 vs $0.99 consensus, revenue $730.8M vs $474.3M expected; company remains profitable and cash-flow positive with ~$1B cash.
EMBARK 3-year topline showed durable, statistically significant motor-function benefit vs external control, supporting the ELEVIDYS efficacy story.
ENDEAVOR Cohort 8 testing sirolimus-based enhanced immunosuppression could materially reduce the acute liver injury risk that broke the stock — a genuine de-risking catalyst.
Valuation is cheap on a franchise basis: fwd P/E ~8.2, EV ~$2.5B against ~$2B revenue; Japan launch adds Roche milestone/royalty upside.
Momentum has turned: +24% over 30 days, +15% over 5 days, trading above the 200-day MA.
bearish_points: Safety overhang is existential — patient deaths tied to gene therapy invite ongoing FDA scrutiny and potential further label restrictions.
Revenue growth is -34% TTM and reported gross margin is negative (-17%), reflecting charges/inventory hits; the P&L is noisy and hard to underwrite.
ELEVIDYS uptake pressured by prescriber caution; recovery depends on the immunosuppression data reading out clean.
Biotech binary risk: a bad safety update could re-break the stock overnight.
catalyst: ENDEAVOR Cohort 8 enhanced-immunosuppression data + continued ELEVIDYS commercial recovery / next quarterly print.
catalyst_timing: Data/updates across H2 2026; next earnings the near-term checkpoint.
suggested_trade: Starter spot position with room to add; risk-tolerant accounts can express via longer-dated calls given event-driven upside.
key_risk: A new ELEVIDYS safety event or FDA action that further restricts the label.
would_skip_if: You can't stomach single-headline binary risk, or the immunosuppression data disappoints.
